title: Correct compression length
description: Essential Criteria: The student's final answer for part (1) must be a length of approximately 0.063 m (or 6.3 cm).

title: Correct passenger count
description: Essential Criteria: The student's final answer for part (2) must be 5 passengers.

title: Apply frequency condition
description: Important Criteria: The solution must set the car's vibration frequency equal to the given human natural frequency of 2 Hz.

title: Use static equilibrium
description: Important Criteria: The solution for part (2) must apply force equilibrium (total weight equals spring force) using Hooke's Law (F = k * l).

title: Correct formula manipulation
description: Important Criteria: The solution must correctly manipulate the given formula f = (1/(2π))√(g/l) to solve for the compression length l.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional Criteria: The solution should demonstrate consistent use of SI units (kg, m, N, Hz) throughout the calculation.

title: Sign or force direction error
description: Pitfall Criteria: Deduct points if the student incorrectly handles the direction of forces in the equilibrium equation, e.g., writing kl = Mg without including passenger weight.

title: Incorrect total mass calculation
description: Pitfall Criteria: Deduct points if the student makes an error in calculating the total mass (car + n*passenger) when applying Hooke's Law.
